canonical.title: Toasts in the Next.js App Router: firing client state from the server

parent.title: React toast notifications in 2026: the landscape, the a11y bill, and the server boundary

siblings.title: React toast libraries in 2026: Sonner, react-toastify, react-hot-toast, notistack and the design-system natives
siblings.summary: Sonner is the 2026 default (41M weekly installs, shadcn's toast); react-toastify is the actively-released power option; react-hot-toast is the 4.7 kB minimalist; notistack is legacy.

siblings.title: Accessible toasts in React (2026): what's actually required, and which libraries deliver
siblings.summary: No React toast library is accessible out of the box: the correct pattern is a pre-mounted live region plus a landmark hotkey, and only Base UI, React Aria and Radix implement it — Sonner is polite-only, react-hot-toast is unreachable by keyboard, notistack fires role=alert into a node that mounts with its own text.

siblings.title: Headless toast primitives vs batteries-included: when rolling your own pays
siblings.summary: Base UI Toast is the only primitive that is both stable and feature-complete in 2026; adopt Sonner unless multi-framework, deep theming, or anchored/custom-queue needs force a primitive.

siblings.title: Migrating off legacy toasts: toastr and react-toastify → Sonner
siblings.summary: toastr is dead (last commit 2018, needs jQuery) — migrate. react-toastify is alive (v11.1.0, Apr 2026) — don't churn a working integration.

sources.title: https://buildui.com/posts/toast-messages-in-react-server-components
sources.claim: Reference implementation of a server-side toast queue in RSC: a Server Function writes a randomly-named toast-<uuid> cookie, a Server Component Toaster reads all of them each render, and a client component dismisses them with useOptimistic plus a Server Function that deletes the cookie.

sources.title: https://www.robinwieruch.de/react-server-actions-useactionstate-toast/
sources.claim: The useActionState + useEffect toast pattern re-toasts stale messages on re-render unless the action's return value carries a timestamp/nonce compared against a ref.

sources.title: https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/functions/redirect
sources.claim: redirect() throws NEXT_REDIRECT, terminates rendering of the segment, serves a 303 when used in a Server Action, and must be called outside try/catch.

sources.title: https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cookies
sources.claim: cookies() is async; .set/.delete are only legal in a Server Function or Route Handler (not during Server Component render); reading cookies opts a route into dynamic rendering; after a cookie write in a Server Function the UI is not unmounted but server-data-dependent effects re-run.

sources.title: https://react.dev/reference/react/useActionState
sources.claim: useActionState returns [state, dispatchAction, isPending]; with Server Functions the initial state and payload must be serializable.

sources.title: https://react.dev/reference/rsc/use-client
sources.claim: 'use client' marks a module boundary: the module and its transitive imports are bundled and evaluated on the client, and props crossing the boundary must be serializable.

sources.title: https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions/67660
sources.claim: Developers report duplicate/stale toasts from useActionState + useEffect, and that a redirecting server action never returns changed state so success cannot be detected; proposed fixes include timestamps and awaiting the action promise directly instead of using useActionState.

sources.title: https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions/77389
sources.claim: The three canonical ways to toast after a redirecting server action are useActionState + router.push, redirect with the message in searchParams, and redirect with the message in a cookie; the thread has no maintainer answer.

sources.title: https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions/57118
sources.claim: Returning a JSON result and calling redirect() in the same server action are mutually exclusive; the recommended workaround is to set a cookie before the redirect and read it on the destination page to show the toast.

sources.title: https://github.com/emilkowalski/sonner/issues/322
sources.claim: Firing a Sonner toast from a useEffect produces two toasts under React StrictMode; the issue is closed as expected React dev-mode behaviour.

sources.title: https://sonner.emilkowal.ski/getting-started
sources.claim: Sonner's <Toaster /> can be rendered directly inside a Next.js server component layout without a hand-written 'use client' wrapper.

sources.title: https://unpkg.com/sonner@2.0.7/dist/index.mjs
sources.claim: sonner 2.0.7 ships 'use client' as the first line of its ESM bundle, so the whole module (Toaster and toast) is a client module.

sources.title: https://unpkg.com/react-hot-toast@2.6.0/dist/index.mjs
sources.claim: react-hot-toast 2.6.0 ships "use client" as the first line of its ESM bundle.

sources.title: https://unpkg.com/react-toastify@11.1.0/dist/index.mjs
sources.claim: react-toastify 11.1.0 ships "use client" as the first line of its ESM bundle.

sources.title: https://github.com/shadcn-ui/ui/issues/8173
sources.claim: shadcn/ui's generated components/ui/sonner.tsx omitted the 'use client' directive while wrapping the Toaster in next-themes' useTheme(), producing a server-component error — re-exporting a client component from a directive-less module erases the boundary.

sources.title: https://bundlephobia.com/package/sonner@2.0.7
sources.claim: sonner 2.0.7 is 34.2 kB minified, 9.4 kB gzipped, with no runtime dependencies.

sources.title: https://bundlephobia.com/package/react-hot-toast@2.6.0
sources.claim: react-hot-toast 2.6.0 is 12.2 kB minified, 4.8 kB gzipped — the smallest of the three.

sources.title: https://bundlephobia.com/package/react-toastify@11.1.0
sources.claim: react-toastify 11.1.0 is 34.4 kB minified, 9.7 kB gzipped.

sources.title: https://reactrouter.com/explanation/sessions-and-cookies
sources.claim: React Router 7's session.flash() writes a value deleted on first read; the action commits the session in the redirect's Set-Cookie header and the loader re-commits it; the docs warn that multiple nested loaders reading the same flash key causes race conditions.

sources.title: https://github.com/remix-run/react-router/discussions/11872
sources.claim: React Router community consensus: session flash is the reliable way to toast after a POST redirect; URL-parameter toasts re-fire on refresh, while flash messages self-destruct on read and so cannot double-toast.

sources.title: https://github.com/code-forge-io/remix-toast
sources.claim: remix-toast is a server-side toast library for React Router v7 / Remix providing redirectWithSuccess-style helpers and getToast returning { toast, headers } for the root loader.

sources.title: https://next-safe-action.dev/docs/execute-actions/hooks/useaction
sources.claim: next-safe-action's useAction hook exposes onSuccess / onError / onSettled callbacks, letting a toast fire from the action result without a useEffect.

sources.title: https://react.dev/reference/react/StrictMode
sources.claim: StrictMode re-runs effects (setup, cleanup, setup) an extra time in development only; production runs the effect once per mount.

sources.title: https://nextjs.org/docs/messages/react-hydration-error
sources.claim: Hydration errors occur when the prerendered React tree differs from the first client render — the risk in toasts comes from server/client-divergent content (dates, locale), not from the empty toaster container itself.

sources.title: https://github.com/TheEdoRan/next-safe-action
sources.claim: next-safe-action provides end-to-end type-safe Server Actions with hooks, validation and callbacks for React/Next.js.
